title: Parents, siblings and the piano at home
summary: His sisters took piano and Lil Armstrong visited the house; his father played banjo; he is the youngest of seven; no other sibling became a professional.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, are either of your parents

Well, I had two sisters. The oldest sister, (unintelligible) L. I The youngest sister was a great friend of Nell Armstrong before she married Louie, and they would come to the house, and my mother would have a beautiful piano because my youngest sister was taking music lessons. But the oldest sister never taken a lesson, so Lil and older sister'd come by and played, and so they get up behind them (unintelligible) and play. So Nell says, well, Josephine, why don't you take lessons? Don't have no time. But she had the better touch than my youngest sister. My youngest sister had a teacher come there to teach her, and oldest sister, Liddy Bowman come down and teach her, but she never acquired caught the taste.
But with me, I would -- I'd say I like the clarinet.
Yeah, but I mean did your father or mother every play an instrument?
My old man used to play fool with the banjo.
Oh, but then how come that -- how many were in your family?
There's three girls and four boys. I'm the youngest of the family.
And did any of the others become professional musicians?
Well, but nevertheless you had this piano home.
Yeah, I had the piano home.
Yeah, did you ever try playing that yourself?
